title: Schematic closure and uniqueness
statement:
Let $i:U\to T$ be a quasi-compact immersion, with $T$ quasi-separated. Its
scheme-theoretic image $\overline U\subseteq T$ is a closed subscheme,
$U\to\overline U$ is an open immersion, and $U$ is scheme-theoretically
dense in $\overline U$.

If $U\subseteq T$ is a scheme-theoretically dense open and $Y\to S$ is
separated, two $S$-maps $T\to Y$ agreeing on $U$ agree on $T$.

Here the scheme-theoretic image means the smallest closed subscheme through which the morphism factors. For an open immersion $j:V\hookrightarrow X$, scheme-theoretic density means that $\mathcal O_X\to j_*\mathcal O_V$ is injective as a morphism of sheaves; no quasi-compactness of $j$ is assumed in the uniqueness assertion.

proof.text: Apply [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-ideal-qc] to $i:U\to T$. It supplies a closed subscheme $\overline U=\operatorname{SIm}(i)\hookrightarrow T$ cut out by the image ideal, together with a factor map $q:U\to\overline U$. By [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-universal], the composite of $q$ and the closed inclusion is $i$, and every other closed factorization admits a unique compatible closed immersion from $\overline U$. Thus this is the smallest closed subscheme through which $i$ factors. The quasi-compactness required for the cited image properties is precisely the hypothesis on $i$.

Apply [lemma-nagata-immersion-open-in-scheme-image] with its $g=i$, source $U$ and target $T$. Its factor map is the map $q$ above. The hypotheses are exactly that $i$ is an immersion and is quasi-compact. It states that $q$ is a quasi-compact open immersion and that its image is scheme-theoretically dense in $\overline U$. To read the density clause in the convention of this statement: in the cited node, $q$ scheme-theoretically dense means that the scheme-theoretic image of $q$ is $\overline U$ itself, i.e. that the ideal of $\mathcal O_{\overline U}$ cut out by the kernel of $\mathcal O_{\overline U}\to q_*\mathcal O_U$ is zero. Since $q$ is quasi-compact, this kernel is already the quasi-coherent kernel ideal of $q$ (the quasi-compact case of the image definition), so the condition says exactly that $\mathcal O_{\overline U}\to q_*\mathcal O_U$ is injective as a morphism of sheaves, which is the density convention stated above for the open immersion $q$. These give the two remaining assertions about the closure, with the full scheme structure retained. No reducedness is assumed and the given quasi-separatedness of $T$ may be retained although this result does not require it.

For the independent uniqueness assertion, write $s:Y\to S$ and $a,b:T\to Y$ for the two $S$-maps and $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ for the schematically dense open. Since both maps are over $S$, $s\circ a=s\circ b$; agreement on $U$ is $a\circ j=b\circ j$. To check schematic dominance, any local section of an ideal sheaf defining a closed factor of $j$ restricts to zero on $U$. Injectivity of $\mathcal O_T\to j_*\mathcal O_U$ forces every such section to be zero. In particular the quasi-coherent kernel ideal of $j$ is zero, which is the schematic dominance condition. Apply [lemma-nagata-ext-scheme-theoretically-dominant-separated] with its $(s,f,g,\iota)=(s,a,b,j)$. Its separatedness assumption is the given separatedness of $Y\to S$, and its conclusion is $a=b$. The kernel check is elementary from sheaf injectivity and the definition of the image ideal; it uses no quasi-compactness of $j$. The cited rigidity theorem needs no reducedness of $T$.
